description: The bar chart compares the accuracy/correlation performance of five different models—Single-task_baseline, Baseline_with_Adaptive_Dropout, Unsupervised_SimCSE, Supervised_SimCSE, and 2-Tier SimCSE—across three evaluation metrics: Sentiment Acc. (sentiment accuracy), STS Corr. (semantic textual similarity correlation), and Paraphrase Acc. (paraphrase accuracy). The vertical axis represents the accuracy/correlation values, ranging from 0 to 0.8, with major gridlines at intervals of 0.2. The horizontal axis lists the five models. For each model, three bars are displayed side-by-side, colored light beige for Sentiment Acc., light red for STS Corr., and light blue for Paraphrase Acc., as indicated by the legend. Across all models, the Paraphrase Acc. consistently achieves the highest accuracy values, followed by STS Corr., and then Sentiment Acc. The 2-Tier SimCSE model demonstrates the highest performance in all three metrics, with Paraphrase Acc. reaching approximately 0.79, STS Corr. around 0.81, and Sentiment Acc. about 0.49. The Single-task_baseline model shows the lowest performance overall, with its highest metric (Paraphrase Acc.) at roughly 0.79, while its Sentiment Acc. is approximately 0.53 and STS Corr. is about 0.50. The Baseline_with_Adaptive_Dropout and Unsupervised_SimCSE models show similar performance, with Paraphrase Acc. around 0.79, STS Corr. around 0.58 and 0.71 respectively, and Sentiment Acc. around 0.52 and 0.52 respectively. The Supervised_SimCSE model performs better than the baseline and unsupervised models, with Paraphrase Acc. at about 0.78, STS Corr. at approximately 0.81, and Sentiment Acc. at around 0.49. The 2-Tier SimCSE model shows a slight improvement over Supervised_SimCSE in STS Corr. and Paraphrase Acc., with values of approximately 0.81 and 0.79 respectively, and a slightly lower Sentiment Acc. of about 0.49.
